name: Question 19
problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨\frac{4}{1+t},\,\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-4t+5⟩.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1.$
worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{4}{1+t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{{t}^{3}}{3}-4t+5)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{(1+t)^{2}},\,{t}^{2}-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{4}{(1+t)^{2}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}-4)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{8}{(1+t)^{3}},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=1,$ we substitute $t=1$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(1) & =⟨\frac{8}{(1+(1))^{3}},\,2(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{8}{{2}^{3}},\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(1)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(1)| & =|⟨1,\,2⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Question 19
?

The position vector r, in meters, of a particle P relative to a fixed origin O at time t seconds is given by r=⟨41+t,t33−4t+5⟩. Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of P at time t=1.

a
5m/s2
b
1m/s2
c
2m/s2
d
3m/s2
e
2m/s2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do this by differentiating the position vector:

v=drdt=⟨dxdt,dydt⟩=⟨ddt(41+t),ddt(t33−4t+5)⟩=⟨−4(1+t)2,t2−4⟩

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(−4(1+t)2),ddt(t2−4)⟩=⟨8(1+t)3,2t⟩

To find the acceleration at time t=1, we substitute t=1 into the above:

a(1)=⟨8(1+(1))3,2(1)⟩=⟨823,2⟩=⟨1,2⟩

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute |a(1)|:

|a(1)|=|⟨1,2⟩|=(1)2+(2)2=5m/s2
